findings.evidence: template/scripts/model_routing.py:1167–1177 handles launcher OSError as an abnormal execution with launched=False. Lines 1251–1254 nevertheless persist a closed platform-observed delegation. The early gate accepts any recorded execution or delegation without checking launch status, and escalate at lines 1010–1020 skips the divergence check whenever a delegation exists. Thus, after an unsuccessful launch, supervisor edits pass routing-adjacent checks and can switch the plan to retention despite no child having run. This contradicts the active delta's requirement for a real recorded delegation or unchanged task content, and design decision 8's requirement that unlaunched preflight failures cannot authorize later supervisor writes or escalation.
findings.summary: An unlaunched Codex failure leaves delegation evidence that permits later supervisor-written content to pass the early gate and authorize escalation.
